questions.question: Q: Name two key developments in ballet during the Renaissance period.

points.text: Ballet originated in the Italian and French courts as court entertainment, and King Louis XIV established the Académie Royale de Danse in 1661, which professionalised ballet training and performance.

questions.question: Q: How did Isadora Duncan challenge the traditions of classical ballet?

points.text: Duncan rejected ballet's rigid technique, corsets and pointe shoes, instead performing barefoot in loose tunics and using natural, expressive movement inspired by ancient Greek art and nature.

questions.question: Q: What was significant about Merce Cunningham's approach to choreography?

points.text: Cunningham used chance procedures such as coin tosses to determine movement order, and he separated dance from music so each could exist independently, breaking the traditional relationship between the two.

questions.question: Q: Describe how hip-hop dance originated and why it matters in dance history.

points.text: Hip-hop dance emerged in the 1970s in the Bronx, New York, among African American and Latino communities as part of hip-hop culture. It introduced breaking, locking and popping, expanding dance beyond studio-based traditions.

questions.question: Q: Why is understanding dance history important for AQA 8236?

points.text: Dance history provides context for the professional works studied in the course, helping students understand choreographic intentions, stylistic influences and how dance has evolved, which supports analysis and appreciation.
